transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you—please come in and have a seat. What brings you in today, and what would you like help with?

For about the past year and a half, maybe closer to two years, I’ve just lost interest in pretty much everything I used to enjoy—hobbies, seeing people, even small things I used to look forward to. It’s gotten to the point where I feel really disconnected from my life, and I don’t know how to get back to feeling like myself, so I wanted to get some help.

In these past 1–2 years, have there been clear periods of at least two months when you felt mostly back to your usual self, or has this low interest and disconnection been present nearly all the time without a real break?
It’s been there pretty much the whole time, just with small day‑to‑day ups and downs. I haven’t had any stretch of a couple of months where I felt like my old self again.

Over the past six months, have you been feeling persistently tense or worried about many different things most days, or is it more that you mainly feel low, disconnected, or without interest but not especially anxious or on edge?

It’s more that I feel low, disconnected, and just not interested in anything, rather than constantly tense or worried about lots of things. I do get anxious sometimes, but it’s not the main thing and it’s not there all the time like the flat, low feeling is.
Along with the loss of interest, how often in the last month have you felt sad, empty, or hopeless most of the day, nearly every day?

Most days I feel more empty and flat than outright sad, and that’s there pretty much all day, almost every day. There are brief moments where I’m distracted and don’t notice it as much, but it always comes back and I rarely feel genuinely hopeful.

Over this past year or two, how much has this low, flat feeling actually interfered with your ability to work, study, or manage daily responsibilities—would you say it has significantly reduced your functioning, or have you mostly been able to keep up, just feeling disconnected while doing so?

It’s definitely reduced my functioning. I still get the basics done, but I’m a lot slower and have a harder time starting things, so I miss deadlines more and let chores pile up unless I really force myself.

In the last couple of weeks, besides low interest and feeling flat, have you also had several other depression symptoms like big changes in sleep or appetite, feeling very guilty or worthless, low energy, trouble concentrating, or thoughts that life isn’t worth living—enough that most days feel like a clearly worse “episode” than your usual baseline over the past two years?

In the last couple of weeks it hasn’t felt like a clearly worse episode; it’s more like the same baseline I’ve had this whole time. I’ve still had very low energy and fatigue, trouble focusing, and a lot of feelings of worthlessness and guilt on most days, and I do sometimes feel like life isn’t really worth much, but that’s all been pretty constant rather than suddenly worse.

When you have those thoughts that life isn’t really worth much, do you ever find yourself wishing you were dead, thinking about harming yourself, or making any plans to end your life, or are these more vague thoughts without any intent or plan?

They’re more vague thoughts, like wondering what the point of things is or thinking it wouldn’t matter much if I just didn’t wake up one day. I don’t have any specific plans or intent to hurt myself, and I haven’t done anything to prepare or act on those thoughts.

Before this past 1–2 years, did you ever have a period of at least two weeks when you suddenly felt much more depressed or lost interest in things than usual, clearly worse than your normal mood at the time, or has it always been more of a long, gradual, and steady low feeling without distinct episodes?

It’s mostly been a long, gradual, steady low feeling without any clear earlier episodes that stand out like this. Before the last couple of years I had ups and downs like anyone, but nothing that felt like a distinct, sustained period of being much more depressed or losing interest for a couple of weeks or more.

Have you ever had a period lasting several days or longer when you felt unusually high, energetic, or irritable, needed much less sleep than usual, and were more talkative or impulsive than your normal self, to the point that others noticed or it caused problems?

I don’t think I’ve ever had anything like that. I’ve had the occasional good day or a short stretch where I felt a bit more motivated, but nothing where I needed much less sleep or was noticeably high or impulsive for several days.

Thinking about the past month or so specifically, does your mood and lack of interest feel clearly worse than it did, say, a year ago—like a noticeable downturn from your usual low baseline—or has it stayed at about the same level of low the whole time without a recent drop?
It feels like it’s stayed at about the same low level rather than taking a noticeable downturn. I can’t really point to any clear recent change in the past month compared with about a year ago.

opening_question.question: Hello, it’s good to meet you—please come in and have a seat. What brings you in today, and what would you like help with?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes a nearly continuous, long‑standing low mood and marked loss of interest lasting about 1.5–2 years, with no periods of two months or more of normal mood, and no distinct prior major depressive episodes. Symptoms include persistent anhedonia, emptiness/flatness, low energy, poor concentration, feelings of worthlessness and guilt, and vague thoughts that life is not worth much, with functional impairment but preserved basic functioning. There is no evidence of manic or hypomanic episodes, and no recent discrete worsening that would define a current major depressive episode. The chronic, subthreshold but impairing depressive picture without clear episodicity is most consistent with dysthymia (persistent depressive disorder) under ICD‑10 F34.1.
